selected_candidates.name: Hex Fiend

build_evidence.official_readme: Native macOS hex editor; local binary editing, searching and comparison.
build_evidence.fixed_source: Makefile invokes xcodebuild for documentation; .gitmodules is empty. Guessed project paths returned HTTP 404, so full project/build dependency admission remains pending.
build_evidence.runtime_expected: macOS AppKit application using local synthetic files; no account needed for proposed core workflows.
limitations: Build, deployment target and signing have not been executed or fully admitted.
Custom byte-grid accessibility may require screenshots and coordinates; macOS AX capability is unverified.
Source archive alone does not include a verified runnable application.

sequence: Observe byte grid, character panel and inspector using a small synthetic binary.
Observe select, replace and save-as state transitions.
Implement the observed editor behavior independently, then reopen and compare saved bytes.
validator_expected: Exact expected byte sequence and file length.
workflows.evidence: Pinned README documents binary editing and inspector; exact task controls require reference UI observation.

sequence: Observe search and compare panels on two small controlled binaries.
Record no-match, next-match and changed-byte states.
Recreate these states, then selfcheck offsets and diff outputs.
validator_expected: No-match state does not mutate data.
workflows.evidence: Pinned README documents search and binary comparison; proposed task contract, not an existing official validator.

skill_expectation: Observe coupled grid/inspector/selection states before recreating a desktop UI.
Treat binary data as bytes and verify saved artifacts.
Separate viewport state from persistent document changes.

bench_correspondence.capability: Structured local editing and state inspection.
Binary editor capabilities on another native platform; strongest functional correspondence.

source_isolation.manual_evidence: Canonical project moved organization; the old owner is treated as an alias.
source_isolation.family_risk: Text/hex editor domain overlap is expected. No exact candidate/alias source identity matched the native catalog, but code similarity is not proven absent.

selected_candidates.name: Gifski
selected_candidates.license: MIT for GUI source; AGPL-3.0-or-later for gifski encoder dependency

build_evidence.official_readme: Convert local videos into GIFs; older compatible v2.23.0 selected rather than current macOS 26 release.
build_evidence.fixed_source: Pinned README says macOS 13+; project deployment target is 13.3. Build uses Xcode, Rust and SwiftLint with Swift package dependencies.
build_evidence.runtime_expected: macOS 14.7.5 reference host can satisfy the declared deployment target; local video/GIF core needs no application account.
limitations: Build/toolchain, signing, Rust library resolution and reference UI not executed.
Dependency revision/license audit must include the AGPL encoder; do not label the whole bundle MIT.
Latest v3 cropping/macOS 26 features are outside selected v2.23.0.
Video decode support and output inspection need admission using a synthetic input.

sequence: Observe local short-video import, settings, preview and save dialog.
Change dimensions, FPS and quality one at a time.
Recreate the observed pipeline and selfcheck decoded GIF dimensions, frame count and saved file.
validator_expected: Expected dimensions and bounded frame count.
Settings visibly update preview and output.
workflows.evidence: Pinned README documents conversion controls; concrete values and preview behavior require UI admission.

sequence: Observe loop, bounce and playback speed behavior on a short synthetic video.
Record reset/new-input transitions.
Implement the observed state handling, then verify animation order and loop metadata.
validator_expected: Expected forward/reverse frame ordering for admitted bounce control.
Replacing source does not export stale frames.
workflows.evidence: Pinned v2 README features; no v3-only crop requirement.

skill_expectation: Map asynchronous media settings to preview and generated artifacts.
Verify output format and metadata in addition to screenshots.
Manage import/export dialogs and stale media state.

bench_correspondence.capability: Local media import, parameter selection, preview and export.
Dimension settings and transformed local image artifacts.
Media parameter changes with persistent output.

source_isolation.manual_evidence: Native Swift GUI is a distinct wrapper around the ImageOptim encoder; both identities are audited against native benchmark sources.
source_isolation.family_risk: Shared codec library/source dependency must be pinned and audited; distinct GUI repo alone does not eliminate transitive source overlap.

selected_candidates.name: MacPass

build_evidence.official_readme: Native macOS KeePass database client; recursive Git checkout, Carthage and Xcode build.
build_evidence.fixed_source: Deployment target 10.13. DDHotKey Git submodule plus Carthage dependencies including KeePassKit, KissXML, TransformerKit, HNHUi and Sparkle.
build_evidence.runtime_expected: Local synthetic password database and dummy values, with no application account or cloud integration.
limitations: Build with recursive dependencies and code signing not yet admitted.
Only GitHub source/release is selected; the project reports abandonment of old macpassapp.org and fixes the update domain in 0.8.2.
AutoType, browser integrations, plugins, external cloud/password stores and real secrets are excluded.
Protocol/source-family risk with benchmark KeeWeb is explicitly unresolved at code/dependency level.

sequence: Observe group and entry forms in an isolated synthetic KeePass database.
Create groups and dummy entries, edit fields, then observe search and selection states.
Independently implement the observed CRUD/search UI and selfcheck local persistence after reopening.
validator_expected: Expected group/entry structure and dummy fields.
workflows.evidence: Pinned README documents local KeePass management; exact forms and validation need UI observation.

sequence: Observe moving an entry between groups and locking/reopening the local database.
Record focus, selection and locked/unlocked state transitions.
Recreate only these admitted behaviors and check that move and lock preserve data.
workflows.evidence: Proposed reference task; lock/move controls and validation must be admitted, without plugins.

skill_expectation: Recreate nested list/detail editors and persistence contracts.
Separate lock/session state from stored records.
Use synthetic fixtures and verify structure instead of memorizing literal passwords.

bench_correspondence.capability: Local structured security records, forms and saved state.
Same KeePass file-format domain; deliberate capability overlap and family-risk disclosure.

source_isolation.manual_evidence: Official README presents MacPass as a native client and KeeWeb as an alternative; no claim of a KeeWeb product fork is present. KeePassKit is a separate dependency.
source_isolation.family_risk: MacPass and benchmark KeeWeb share KeePass/KDBX format and may share algorithms or libraries. This supports capability transfer but does not establish strict family isolation. A family/source dependency review is required before accepting strong isolation claims.

selected_candidates.download_size: Root acquired source archive; use root acquisition manifest for exact bytes. No source download or build by this subagent.

selected_candidates.name: Fossify Gallery

build_evidence.fixed_source: compileSdk 36, targetSdk 36, minSdk 26; foss/gplay flavors. Main manifest removes ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE; merged APK manifest not audited.

sequence: Observe seeded local album/list/detail states and file picker permissions.
Observe a controlled rotate or resize operation and save result.
Recreate these states and check resulting image orientation/dimensions plus local file persistence.
validator_expected: Saved artifact readable in local album.
Album selection and new-media refresh are consistent.
workflows.evidence: Pinned README lists local gallery/editing; exact controls and permissions need reference UI admission.

sequence: Observe creating/renaming an album and moving selected synthetic images.
Observe delete-to-recycle and restore states if supported by selected UI.
Implement admitted list-selection/dialog/storage transitions and compare expected filenames and membership.
validator_expected: Admitted recycle/restore operation preserves controlled bytes.
workflows.evidence: Proposed task from pinned gallery/recycle-bin capabilities; confirm selected release UI before task freeze.

skill_expectation: Observe Android scoped-storage and multi-selection flows.
Recreate media list/detail/editor transitions with persistent files.
Validate generated artifacts and list refresh, not only image similarity.

bench_correspondence.capability: Local image selection and generated file outputs.
Albums/files, selection, move and permission dialogs.

selected_candidates.name: Activity Diary

build_evidence.official_readme: Local activity tracking, notes, pictures and history; privacy policy says data stays local unless the user requests transmission.
build_evidence.fixed_source: compileSdk 30, targetSdk 30, minSdk 21; applicationId de.rampro.activitydiary. Older Gradle/dependencies include map, charts and optional mail crash reporting.
build_evidence.runtime_expected: Local activity/notes/history workflows without account, location lookup, maps or crash-report transmission.
limitations: Old Android build toolchain/dependency repository and API 35 runtime compatibility not admitted.
Publishing Gradle configuration refers to a service-account file; publishing tasks are excluded, and debug configuration must be checked without any credential.
No installation/UiAutomator testing has occurred.
Timing-sensitive numeric duration scoring is avoided; deterministic activity/notes/history state is proposed.

sequence: Observe creating activities, choosing color/icon and current-activity selection.
Observe start/change/stop states and adding a short synthetic note.
Recreate the admitted state machine, then verify selected activity, note content and history sequence.
validator_expected: Expected note attached to correct event.
History order agrees with observed transitions.
workflows.evidence: Pinned README and local privacy policy; exact forms/buttons need UI observation.

sequence: Observe activity search/filter and editing a controlled history note.
Record empty-result and restored-list states.
Independently implement these transitions and selfcheck persistence after reopening.
validator_expected: Empty search does not delete stored records.
workflows.evidence: Proposed task; search/edit availability must be admitted in selected release.

skill_expectation: Infer a timer/activity state machine from observable transitions.
Implement local CRUD/filtering and history persistence.
Avoid treating wall-clock timing noise as task success evidence.

bench_correspondence.capability: Local planning records and multiple screens.

source_isolation.manual_evidence: Official project has its own Activity Diary implementation; exact repository identities were compared across all public benchmark source rows.
source_isolation.family_risk: Functional domain overlaps timer/planning benchmark apps. Exact identity non-overlap is not a source-copy or full product-lineage guarantee.

rejected.reason: Current macOS 26/toolchain mismatch; README places image assets under CC-BY-NC-ND-4.0 despite Apache source. Not admitted as wholly open asset pool.
compileSdk/targetSdk 37.2; selected older v1.2 declares SDK 35. Initial evidence/manifest retained.

limits: All six are source-acquisition candidates, not runnable/admitted fixtures.
GitHub anonymous API requests returned 403; no API-derived fork/archive flag is asserted. Fixed SHA evidence came from git ls-remote and pinned raw docs.
Public native catalog covers 200 source repositories/commits; web 50 rows have no public source identity. Exact non-match alone cannot prove family isolation.
Reference GUI observations, independent task validators, merged dependency/license audit and source-similarity audit remain required before training.

RecreationWorld-style proposal: observe reference GUI states, independently implement original code, selfcheck generated app/artifacts. Proposed workflows describe reference interactions and expected checks, not authorization to execute.
